accepted.dr200s-2017-service: REVIEWED 2026-09-01 (fleet lap 1, beat 6) — ACCEPTED, on Paul's ruling: "we just have one motorcycle. You should have the VIN so you determine what it is. It's 200 SE or 200 S, and make that canonical, no confusion." ⭐ CANONICAL DESIGNATION IS **DR200S** — the card was already right. Reasoning, with its grades separated: (a) DETERMINISTIC — the VIN on record, JS1SH42A4H2••••••, gives Suzuki/Japan, model code SH42A, Hamamatsu, and model-year letter H = 2017. (b) NOT FROM THE VIN — the SH42A code spans the DR200SE/DR200S family and does NOT by itself split SE from S. What splits them is the MODEL YEAR: Suzuki sold this machine in the US as the DR200SE through the earlier generation and as the DR200S from the 2015 re-release, so a 2017 is a DR200S. That half is model-designation knowledge, not a read off the VIN, and it is graded as such. So the service manual's 'DR200SE' is the SAME machine under the earlier / service-literature designation — one machine, two names, and the document is usable. Falsifier: any DR200SE-specific value that disagrees with a DR200S spec.

The card's Z254F is carried on its own evidence (the trim names the Kawasaki FR691V), not on this ruling.
